title: A Deep Learning-Driven Operator Splitting Scheme for Free Boundary Problems: An Application to American Option Pricing in Incomplete Markets
abstract: arXiv:2610.36921v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: This paper proposes a deep learning-driven operator splitting scheme for high-dimensional free-boundary problems, with American option pricing as a representative application. In a market with proportional transaction costs, a stochastic liquidity risk with an empirically validated nonlinear drift based on S&P 500 data, and two-factor stochastic volatility, the pricing problem takes the form of a five-dimensional highly nonlinear variational inequality. The proposed scheme decomposes this variational inequality at each time layer into an elliptic continuation equation approximated by a physics-informed neural network and a closed-form projection step enforcing the early-exercise constraint. A conditional $\ell^\infty$ stability bound is derived under stated resolvent and Lipschitz assumptions. translated_title: 一种面向自由边界问题的深度学习驱动算子分裂格式：在非完全市场中美式期权定价的应用
translated_abstract: 本文提出了一种针对高维自由边界问题的深度学习驱动的算子分裂格式，并以美式期权定价作为代表性应用。在一个包含比例交易成本、基于标普500数据经实证验证的非线性漂移的随机流动性风险、以及两因子随机波动率的市场中，定价问题表现为一个五维高度非线性的变分不等式。所提出的格式在每个时间层将该变分不等式分解为一个由物理信息神经网络近似的椭圆延拓方程，以及一个强制执行提前行权约束的闭式投影步骤。在给定的预解算子和Lipschitz假设条件下，推导出了条件 ℓ^∞ 稳定性界。该格式通过与有限差分和最小二乘蒙特卡洛基准方法的对比进行了验证，包括期权价格和所学习到的行权边界……（原文摘要不完整，此处为可用部分的翻译）
tldr: 本文提出一种深度学习驱动的算子分裂格式，将高维自由边界问题（如非完全市场中美式期权定价对应的五维非线性变分不等式）在每个时间层分解为由物理信息神经网络近似的椭圆延拓方程与强制提前行权约束的闭式投影步骤，并推导出条件稳定性界，其结果与有限差分和最小二乘蒙特卡洛基准高度吻合。
en_tdlr: This paper proposes a deep learning-driven operator splitting scheme that decomposes high-dimensional free-boundary problems—such as the five-dimensional nonlinear variational inequality arising from American option pricing in incomplete markets—at each time layer into a physics-informed neural network approximation of an elliptic continuation equation and a closed-form projection step enforcing the early-exercise constraint, with a conditional stability bound derived and validation against finite-difference and least-squares Monte Carlo benchmarks.
